title: Build fuzz-driven shadow metering replay harness for websocket captures to validate idempotency and rate-limiter state transitions
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Problem: We observe sporadic mismatches between the serving runtime's reported token output and the billing ledger for resumed websocket sessions and replayed client fragments. Root causes include out-of-order delivery, proxy-induced reserialization, and transient speculative outputs from the model. Existing unit/integration tests cover deterministic scenarios but do not exercise the combinatorial replay/reordering space we see in production captures.

Goal: Implement a shadow metering replay harness that: 1) ingests anonymized websocket capture logs from production, 2) replays streams deterministically into a replicated metering pipeline that mirrors production runtime semantics, 3) runs a fuzz engine that injects reorders, truncations, duplicate frames, speculative-output toggles, and midstream model-switch events, and 4) verifies invariants (idempotent final credits, consistent token counts between runtime and ledger, and correct rate-limiter state transitions). The harness should produce actionable diffs and tie failures back to minimal repros that can be filed as follow-up ENG tickets.

Acceptance criteria:
- Shadow harness can load and replay at least three anonymized websocket capture families (editor sessions, mobile offline-reupload, and multiplexed-proxy traces) and run fuzz mutations against them.
- For each replay, verifier checks token-count parity (per-request and per-session), ledger idempotency (replayed sequence produces no net double-debit), and rate-limiter state alignment (limits/quotas after replay match expected final state).
- Harness produces a normalized failure artifact: (minimal mutated trace + golden expected ledger snapshot + runtime logs + suggested blame window).
- End-to-end fuzz runs run in CI as a nightly job against a representative sample and block release if any high-severity assertion fails.

Implementation notes:
- We will reuse the existing session-capture ingest format (proto V2) and add a lightweight anonymizer pipeline (remove customer IDs, strip attachments, truncate long texts).
- The shadow metering pipeline should be implemented as a library that can be invoked locally and as a k8s Job for scale. It must not touch production billing ledgers; instead it writes to an isolated test ledger instance and a local verification store.
- Fuzz engine: start with a small mutation DSL (reorder N frames, drop N frames, duplicate frame, simulate reconnect with new session ID, midstream model switch event, speculative-output toggle, compress/fragment attachments). Mutations should be deterministic given a seed to enable reproducible minimal repro extraction.
- Verifier invariants: final token tally per session, first-debit timestamp monotonicity, rate-limiter allowance reconciliation, and idempotent net-debit (replays vs baseline).

Risks and mitigations:
- Risk: replay harness diverges from production runtime semantics and produces false positives. Mitigation: pair with runtime engineers to port critical runtime hooks (tokenizer version, pretokenizer flags, speculative decoding policy) into the harness as configuration knobs.
- Risk: PII exposure when using captures. Mitigation: mandatory anonymizer step and policy that only sanitized artifacts are allowed in CI.

Rollout plan:
1) Prototype as a local binary and run against synthetic captures within two sprints.
2) Integrate anonymizer and CI nightly job, run on a small production sample (sanitized).
3) Expand mutation set, stabilize failure artifact format, and add alerting for regression severity.
4) On success, add a new ownership runbook and route high-confidence failures into automated Linear templates for triage.

Links to artifacts:
- Design doc (Confluence): https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/METER/Fuzz+Replay+Harness
- Initial prototyping PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/4821
- Anonymizer script: gs://redwood-artifacts/anonymizers/ws-anon-v1.py

Notes: This ticket intentionally avoids changing production billing paths; it is a safety valve used to detect and reproduce correctness gaps before any ledger-affecting fix is deployed.
